synopsis: The camera remains a candidate rather than a confirmed sensor for the heavy off-road braking system; the research therefore covers multiple sensing modalities, whose weather-related failures differ [f2035, f6625, f11303]. Camera and lidar logs with accurate poses support replay and near-path novel-view simulation, but camera logs cannot recover radar or ultrasonic responses, and injected video bypasses physical camera components rather than revalidating them [f80, f84, f5286]. Validation still needs physical correlation for optics, processing, contamination, vibration, glare, darkness and precipitation: visually convincing RGB output and simulator input specifications do not establish detector-level accuracy [f490, f1737, f4558, f3940]. Caterpillar warns of missed crouching or lying people and impaired detection in low light or snow, rain and fog; NIOSH's 2022 review also reported snow and grime degradation in off-road work [f1638, f10557]. UniSim (2023) and S2R-Bench (December 2025) show camera sim-to-real gaps, especially in adverse weather; no published validated camera dust model with a reported error metric was found, and fidelity for the exact units remains uncertain [f329, f254, f8174]. A December 2024 RGB–lidar excavation de-dusting study scored 65.58% in one far-dense-dust case versus 94.85–96.73% in other cases of that scenario, while evidence that pairwise or three-way coverage suffices for coupled sensor failures remains unproven [f10564, f6827].
